reasons: No automated visual or layout test is visible.
The file header says it was generated, so hand edits may be lost if it is regenerated.
The packet's section labels do not match which rules are screen-width specific.

terms.meaning: The language that sets how a web page looks, such as colours, sizes, and spacing.
A rule that applies only when the screen is a certain width or the device has a certain setting.
A named colour or font value that many rules reuse, so a change happens in one place.
A device setting that asks apps to show less animation.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Scope and default look
sections.what: Sets the colours, fonts, and spacing values for the landing area. It also sets the default background, text colour, and font, and the safe area padding for phones with notches. Every rule starts with the scope marker, so other pages are not affected.
sections.why: Likely reason: the scope marker keeps these styles from changing the rest of the app.
sections.watch_out: The file header says it was generated, so manual edits here may be overwritten if the generator runs again.

sections.name: @media (prefers-color-scheme:dark)
sections.title: Dark colours and base styles
sections.what: Defines a dark colour set that applies when the device prefers dark mode, unless the user chose light on the site. A second dark rule applies when the user chose dark on the site. The block then styles links, buttons, focus outlines, the top bar, the logo mark, and the navigation.
sections.why: Likely reason: users can choose light or dark, and the site setting overrides the device setting.
sections.watch_out: The light override depends on the theme attribute that the root layout's script sets on the page root, so a missing script silently falls back to the device setting.

sections.name: @media (max-width:880px)
sections.title: Hides navigation on narrow screens
sections.what: On screens 880 pixels wide or narrower, the top navigation links are hidden. The rest of this section styles the buttons, the hero heading, the tease box, and the redacted name effect, where a dark bar slides away to reveal a name.
sections.why: Likely reason: there is not enough room for the navigation links on a narrow screen, so they are removed.
sections.watch_out: On narrow screens the top navigation disappears entirely, so visitors must use buttons and page content to move around.

sections.name: @media (max-width:860px)
sections.title: Stacks the hero and sport cards
sections.what: Below 860 pixels, the hero switches from two columns to one. The rest of this section styles the sport card row, the coloured bands and captions, and the rise animation that brings each card in.
sections.why: Likely reason: a two-column hero does not fit a narrow screen, and the animation gives the card row a gentle entrance.
sections.watch_out: The cards start hidden and only appear through this animation, so breaking the animation can hide them.

sections.name: @media (max-width:640px)
sections.title: Sport card row on small phones
sections.what: Below 640 pixels, the sport card row becomes a horizontal strip that the user can scroll, with each card snapping into place. The rest of this section sets section spacing, the section heading layout, and the lead text, which apply at every width.
sections.why: Likely reason: five cards would be too cramped on a small phone, so they scroll instead.
sections.watch_out: The strip uses negative margins to reach the screen edges, so changes to page padding can make it misalign.

sections.name: @media (max-width:760px)
sections.title: Narrow section headings and panels
sections.what: Below 760 pixels, the section heading stacks into one column. The rest of this section styles the panels, the desk header, the segmented toggle, the brief rows, rank numbers, sparkline charts, and score numbers, and these apply at every width.
sections.why: Likely reason: the brief rows and headings need a clear layout that works on both wide and narrow screens.
sections.watch_out: The brief rows use a fixed width for the swing column, which can crowd the text on narrow screens.

sections.name: @media (max-width:760px) (part 1)
sections.title: Brief rows and call area
sections.what: Below 760 pixels, the brief rows get a simpler two-column layout, sparklines are narrower, and the image is hidden. The rest of this section, which applies at every width, styles the tabs, the scenario text, the fact boxes, the option buttons, the lock row, and the reveal area with its bars and grade.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the call-making screen usable on smaller screens, since it is the main interactive area.
sections.watch_out: The packet labels this whole range as narrow-screen only, but most rules here apply at every width.

sections.name: @media (max-width:760px) (part 2)
sections.title: Results ledger and notes
sections.what: Styles the results list, with each line showing a label and a value in a bordered row, and styles the small note text used under panels.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The packet labels this as a narrow-screen rule, but it applies at every width.

sections.name: @media (max-width:900px)
sections.title: Stacks call and reveal on medium screens
sections.what: Below 900 pixels, the call area and the reveal area each switch to one column, and the scorecard moves below its content with a top border.
sections.why: Likely reason: side-by-side panels do not fit a medium width, so they stack.

sections.name: @media (max-width:560px)
sections.title: Compact options and card styles
sections.what: Below 560 pixels, the option buttons and fact boxes go to one column, and the tabs get smaller padding with the small status text hidden. Below that, the card grid and card text styles apply at every width.
sections.why: Likely reason: small phones need larger tap targets and less text in the tabs.
sections.watch_out: The packet labels the card rules as narrow-screen only, but they sit outside the width rule and apply everywhere.

sections.name: @media (max-width:1100px)
sections.title: Three-column cards on tablets
sections.what: Below 1100 pixels, the card grid shows three cards per row instead of five.
sections.why: Likely reason: five cards would be too narrow on a tablet-sized screen.

sections.name: @media (max-width:720px)
sections.title: Single column cards and dossier
sections.what: Below 720 pixels, cards stack in one column with a small coloured band on the side. The rest of this section, which applies at every width, styles the file grid and the dossier card with its redacted name, revealed name, details grid, and the copy message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dossier card is a signature element that must work on small phones too.
sections.watch_out: The packet labels this section as narrow-screen only, but the dossier styles apply at every width.

sections.name: @media (max-width:860px)
sections.title: Stacked file grid
sections.what: Below 860 pixels, the file grid switches to one column. The rest of this section sets up the grid for the profile panels and the heading style, which apply at every width.
sections.why: Likely reason: two side-by-side columns are too tight on medium screens.

sections.name: @media (max-width:700px)
sections.title: Single column profiles
sections.what: Below 700 pixels, the profile grid goes to one column. The rest of this section styles the three-step list with coloured top borders, its numbers, and its headings, which apply at every width.
sections.why: Likely reason: profile blocks need more room than a narrow width allows.

sections.name: @media (max-width:760px)
sections.title: Steps in one column
sections.what: Below 760 pixels, the three-step list shows in one column. The rest of this section styles the footer with its border, spacing, and text colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: three steps side by side would be too narrow on phones.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)
sections.title: Reduced motion and last details
sections.what: For people who prefer reduced motion, all animations and transitions in the landing area are turned off. The rest of this section sets the minimum page height, the bar growth animation used for the score bars, the top action spacing, and the footer link colour.
sections.why: Likely reason: some people get dizzy or distracted by motion, so the device setting is respected.
sections.watch_out: The bar growth animation is switched off under reduced motion, so bars will show their final size at once.

summary: Stylesheet for the landing area, with colours for light and dark mode and layout rules for each screen width.
purpose: Makes the public landing area look right on phones, tablets, and desktops, in light or dark mode, without changing other pages.
why: Every rule starts with the scope marker, so the styles only touch the landing area. The file header says it was generated from a published design concept.
how: Steps in order: the file first sets the colours, fonts, and spacing values for the landing area. Then it sets the dark colour set, used when the device or the site setting asks for dark. Then it styles the base elements: links, buttons, focus outlines, the top bar, the logo mark, the navigation, the hero, the sport card row, the sections, the call area, the reveal area, the file grid, the steps, and the footer. Width rules adjust these for smaller screens. A final rule turns off motion for people who prefer less motion.
inputs: The class names on landing page elements, the theme setting saved in the browser, the device's dark mode setting, the device's motion setting, and the screen width.
outputs: The visual look of the landing area.
risks: The packet labels several sections with screen-width rules, but many rules inside those ranges apply at every width, so a change in the wrong place can affect more screens than intended. The colours and fonts depend on font files loaded by the root layout.
debug: If colours look wrong, check the theme setting and the device dark mode setting. If the top navigation disappears, check the rule for screens 880 pixels or narrower. If sport cards are invisible, check the rise animation and the motion setting. Use the browser's element inspector to see which rule is winning.
